# Reuse audit

<!-- The tables between GENERIERT:START and GENERIERT:ENDE are generated by tools/build.py from data/core/audits/. Change them there, not here. The rest of the text is written by hand. -->
## Purpose and scope
The reuse audit records existing building components that are affected by a conversion or deconstruction and are to be examined for reuse.

For this purpose, project, building and component data are recorded in a report. These data are to form the basis for selecting which components should be placed with internal or external takers.

Where needed, the recording can be done in two stages. Stage I is a rough assessment of whether the building fabric under consideration is suitable for reuse and therefore for an in-depth survey in stage II. It also narrows down the component groups for which an in-depth survey in stage II is recommended.

Stage II is an in-depth survey of the components. It can be chosen on the basis of the stage I recommendation or without a preliminary assessment. The aim of stage II is to select suitable components for placement with takers.
## Level of consideration and structure
To structure the reuse audit, it must be defined how the undertaking is divided into projects, buildings and component catalogues.

First, the perimeter of the building fabric concerned, including the surrounding outdoor space and any construction stages, should be stated as precisely as possible.

Combining several buildings into one project makes sense, for example, when the buildings are deconstructed or converted in the same period and a common component catalogue can be considered across the objects.

For each project, the project data and participants are to be recorded once according to table X: «Data fields Project».

For all buildings of a project, the building data are to be recorded according to table X: «Data fields Donor buildings». For identical or connected buildings, these can be combined and stated once.

The extent to which component data are recorded differs between stages I and II of the reuse audit and is set out in the following sections. The structure and levels of consideration of the components are not prescribed by Swiss Inv.
## Reuse audit stage I: aim and procedure
The reuse audit stage I provides a rough estimate of the reuse potential of the components of a donor building. It allows a first assessment of whether, and to what extent, an in-depth examination makes sense. For a survey that meets the need, the client's objectives and the perimeter of the building fabric concerned should be communicated to the auditor before the site visit.

The assessment of potential forms the basis for a targeted, needs-based deepening of the examination. In particular, the component groups relevant to an in-depth examination are to be narrowed down.

On completion of the audit, the client receives a report that serves as a basis for deciding the following questions:

- Should a reuse audit stage II be carried out for the donor building examined?

- Which component groups should be recorded and assessed in depth as part of the reuse audit stage II?

Once the report is complete, the results should be aligned with the client's objectives and resources in order to decide how to proceed.
## Reuse audit stage I: format and scope
The reuse audit stage I comprises the following sections:

- Project: details of the project and the project participants

- Introduction: project description, objectives, dates, perimeter, basis documents (e.g. plans / pollutant report) and the auditor's procedure

- Buildings: details of the donor buildings considered

- Components: rough recording of all components, each with the recommendation for or against an in-depth survey

- Conclusion: reasoned recommendation for or against a reuse audit stage II of the donor buildings considered

The format of the deliverable is to be agreed between client and auditor. Delivering the whole report as a PDF is recommended.

The project and building data are to be recorded in accordance with the section «Level of consideration and structure».

For the project and the donor buildings, at least the information in the following table is to be recorded.

For each component, at least the information marked «Must» in the column «Obligation» of table X: «Information to be recorded per component in the reuse audit stage I» is to be recorded. The column «Data field» recommends suitable data fields from table Y: «Data fields Reuse components», which should be used for this information.

The **quantity** of the components may be given approximately as a range. To keep the lower and upper limits of the range machine-readable, the data fields Quantity (min) and Quantity (max) must be given as numbers. A verified quantity can be indicated by entering the same quantity in both data fields.

An **assessment of pollutant contamination** with regard to reuse is not part of the minimum requirements for reuse audits stage I.

**Further properties** of the components are to be recorded as text in the data field «Further information» or in other suitable data fields. For optimal data exchange, the standardised data fields from table Y: «Data fields Reuse components» are to be preferred for this.

<!-- GENERIERT:START profil=stage-1 bereich=bauteile -->
**Table: information to be recorded per component in the Reuse audit stage I**

| Information | Obligation | Data field | Key | Format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Short name | Must | Name | `name` | Free text (single line) |
| eBKP-H | Must | eBKP-H code | `ebkphCode` | Code list |
|  |  | eBKP-H label | `ebkphLabel` | Free text (single line) |
| Quantity, approximate where necessary, stating the uncertainty | Must | Quantity (min) | `quantityMin` | Number |
|  |  | Quantity (max) | `quantityMax` | Number |
|  |  | Unit | `unit` | Code list |
| At least one material category | Must | Material category | `material` | Code list (multiple choice) |
| Further information | Should | Further information | `description` | Free text (multi-line) |
| Recommendation for or against an in-depth survey | Must | Recommendation detailed survey | `recDetailedAssessment` | Code list |
<!-- GENERIERT:ENDE -->

Definitions and formats of the data fields are given in the [data dictionary](../dictionary/EN.md).

## Reuse audit stage II: aim and procedure
The reuse audit stage II prepares the placement of the components with internal or external takers. For a survey that meets the need, the client's objectives and the perimeter of the building fabric concerned should be communicated to the auditor before the site visit.

On completion of the audit, the client receives a report on the basis of which it can be decided which components should be made visible for placement.

The information recorded should be reusable at least for an informal clarification of demand with potential takers. Depending on the placement strategies and channels, additional detailed clarifications on components may be required.

Developing the placement strategies, managing the placement channels and additional clarifications for placement are not part of the reuse audit stage II. These services, which build on the audit, are not standardised by Swiss Inv.

Once the report is complete, the results should be aligned with the client's objectives and resources in order to decide how to proceed.
## Reuse audit stage II: format and scope
The reuse audit stage II comprises the following sections:

- Project: details of the project and the project participants

- Introduction: project description, objectives, dates, perimeter, basis documents (e.g. plans / pollutant report) and the auditor's procedure

- Buildings: details of the donor buildings considered

- Components: in-depth survey of all components, each with the recommendation for or against placement

- Conclusion: summary of the results

The format of the deliverable is to be agreed between client and auditor. Delivering the whole report as a PDF, the recorded components in a tabular data format, and the image files of buildings and components is recommended.

The project and building data are to be recorded in accordance with the section «Level of consideration and structure».

For the project and the donor buildings, at least the information in the following table is to be recorded.

For each component, at least the information marked «Must» in the column «Obligation» of table X: «Information to be recorded per component in the reuse audit stage II» is to be recorded. The column «Data field» recommends suitable data fields from table Y: «Data fields Reuse components», which should be used for this information.

The **quantity** of the components is to be given precisely. A verified quantity can be indicated by giving the same value in Quantity (min) and Quantity (max).

An **assessment of pollutant contamination** with regard to reuse is not part of the minimum requirements for reuse audits stage II. The auditor must state in the data field «Pollutant report» whether an assessment of contamination by a pollutant report exists for the component concerned. Further details on the author and date of the pollutant report and on the type and degree of contamination are optional. The implications of a pollutant assessment for the reuse of the component may only be interpreted by pollutant specialists.

At least one **main photo** must be provided for each component. In addition, at least two further photos should be taken that add useful information on details or overviews. The assignment of photos or other attachments to the components concerned should be ensured by suitable file naming.

Besides the required fields, **further properties** can be recorded in suitable additional data fields. For optimal data exchange, the standardised data fields from table Y: «Data fields Reuse components» are to be preferred for this.
